subject: Science
title: Science Exam 4
topic: Health & Lifestyle · Periodic Table · Investigative skills
intro: AQA Higher style. Write full sentences for the longer answers. Use the number of marks as a guide to how many points to make.

questions.q: Which reagent turns blue-black when starch is present?
questions.ms: Iodine solution (orange-brown to blue-black).

questions.q: What is a positive result for the Biuret test for protein?
questions.ms: Blue to purple/lilac.

questions.q: Describe how a student could test a food sample for sugar (glucose). Give the positive result.
questions.ms: 1 mark each: add Benedict's solution to the food sample (in solution); heat in a hot water bath (about 80 °C) for a few minutes; positive result: blue changes to green, yellow, orange or brick red.

questions.q: Give the role of fibre and the role of protein in a balanced diet.
questions.ms: Fibre: keeps food moving through the gut / prevents constipation (1). Protein: growth and repair of cells and tissues (1).

questions.q:
Ali is 14 and plays football every day. His uncle is 45 and works in an office.
Explain why Ali and his uncle need different amounts of energy from their food each day. Give other factors that affect how much energy a person needs.
questions.ms: Up to 4: Ali is more active, so his muscles use more energy (1); he is still growing, so needs energy/protein for growth (1); other factors (1 each, max 2): body mass/size, sex, pregnancy, climate/keeping warm, age.

questions.q:
Yassin eats a cheese sandwich. The bread contains starch and the cheese contains fat and protein.
Describe how the food is digested and absorbed as it passes through the digestive system. Name the enzymes involved.
questions.ms: Level 3 (5-6): detailed, logical sequence through the organs with enzymes and products, and absorption. Level 2 (3-4): several organs and enzymes, some links. Level 1 (1-2): simple points. Points: teeth break food into smaller pieces (bigger surface area); saliva contains amylase, which starts breaking starch into sugars; oesophagus moves food by peristalsis; stomach acid kills bacteria, protease starts digesting protein into amino acids; bile from the liver breaks fat into droplets; in the small intestine amylase, protease and lipase finish digestion (fat to fatty acids and glycerol); small molecules are absorbed through villi into the blood; large intestine absorbs water.

questions.q: Which enzyme breaks down protein?
questions.ms: Protease (proteins to amino acids).

questions.q: Enzymes are described as biological catalysts. Explain what this means.
questions.ms: Speed up reactions (in the body) (1) without being used up / changed themselves (1).

questions.q: Describe two ways that bacteria in the large intestine help the body.
questions.ms: Any two: help break down / digest fibre; make vitamins (e.g. vitamin K); stop harmful bacteria growing (compete with them).

questions.q: Describe the effects of smoking cigarettes on the body. Refer to tar, nicotine and carbon monoxide in your answer.
questions.ms: 1 mark each, max 4: tar coats the lungs/alveoli and can cause cancer; tar damages cilia so mucus and germs build up (coughs, bronchitis); nicotine is addictive; nicotine raises heart rate/blood pressure; carbon monoxide reduces the oxygen the blood can carry (so less oxygen for respiration).

questions.q: A lack of a mineral or vitamin in the diet causes poor growth or illness. What is the name for this?
questions.ms: Deficiency.

questions.q: Which element is in Group 1 and Period 3 of the periodic table?
questions.ms: Sodium.

questions.q: Give two physical properties of metals that most non-metals do not have.
questions.ms: Any two: good conductors of electricity; good conductors of heat; shiny; malleable; ductile; high density; sonorous; high melting point.

Predict the melting point of rubidium.
questions.ms: Any value between 30 and 62 °C (actual 39 °C).

questions.q:
Potassium reacts with water. It fizzes, moves around on the surface and burns with a lilac flame.
Predict how rubidium would react with water. Explain your answer and name the products.
questions.ms: Reacts more vigorously/violently than potassium, may explode (1); because reactivity increases down Group 1 (1); products: rubidium hydroxide (1) and hydrogen (1). Allow: the solution is alkaline.

questions.q: Describe how the colour, melting point and reactivity of the Group 7 elements (halogens) change as you go down the group.
questions.ms: Colour gets darker (1); melting/boiling point increases (1); reactivity decreases (1).

questions.q: Chlorine is bubbled into potassium bromide solution. A more reactive halogen displaces a less reactive one. Name the halogen that is displaced.
questions.ms: Bromine (chlorine is more reactive than bromine).

questions.q: Explain why the Group 0 elements (noble gases) are very unreactive, and give one use that depends on this.
questions.ms: They have a full outer shell of electrons (so they do not gain, lose or share electrons) (1). Use: helium in balloons / argon in light bulbs / neon in signs (1).

questions.q:
A student burns a crisp under a test tube of water and records the temperature rise. She repeats it three times.
RepeatTemperature rise (°C)
124
227
324
Calculate the mean temperature rise.

The student then burns different foods to compare how much energy they release.
Name the independent variable, the dependent variable and one control variable.
questions.ms: Independent: type of food (1). Dependent: temperature rise of the water (1). Control (1): mass of food; volume of water; distance from flame to tube; starting temperature of water; same tube.

questions.q: Which type of graph should the student use to show the temperature rise for each different food?
questions.ms: Bar chart, because the type of food is categoric data.

questions.q: Suggest one reason why the temperature rise is lower than the true energy in the food, and one way to improve the experiment.
questions.ms: Reason (1): heat lost to the air / surroundings or the tube; food not fully burnt. Improvement (1): put a shield/insulation around it, keep the food close to the tube, make sure it burns completely.
